# Review: C-401 Debutanizer Narrative, Section 5.1

**Verdict: Do not issue for configuration.** There are two blocking defects:

1. **The TIC-405 action statement contradicts itself.** If it is configured as written, the loop runs open-loop unstable.
2. **The tuning values in the narrative conflict with the issued tuning sheet.** They should not be in the narrative at all.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | ¶2, TIC-405 action | **Blocking.** "Reverse acting" means output decreases as PV rises. The sentence then says a temperature rise *increases* steam flow, which is direct action. More steam on high temperature drives temperature higher still: positive feedback. The correct behavior is less steam on a temperature rise, which is reverse action. The label is right and the description is wrong. A configurer could follow either one. | State one behavior: "When TT-405 increases, TIC-405 decreases the FIC-420 setpoint (reverse action)." Witness the direction at FAT with a simulated PV step. |
| R-02 | ¶5, TIC-405 tuning | **Blocking.** The narrative says Kc = 0.8, Ti = 12 min. The issued tuning sheet says Kc = 1.2, Ti = 8 min. Two sources give two answers. Tuning values do not belong in an FRS. | Delete the tuning sentence. Reference the tuning sheet by document number and revision. The tuning sheet owner should confirm that last month's sheet is current. Do not resolve this by editing the narrative. |
| R-03 | ¶6, TT-405 failure | "Should hold approximately its last output" cannot be tested. "Should" is not a requirement. "Approximately" has no tolerance. The text does not say how bad PV is detected or what FIC-420 does. It also leaves the alarm, operator prompt, and return-to-cascade path undefined. | Specify the full sequence: bad PV detection, TIC-405 mode change, output freeze (hold last good value), FIC-420 mode shed, alarm (by reference), and operator action to restore. See the rewrite below. |
| R-04 | ¶7, FIC-420 manual | "May… during upsets" is permission, not a requirement. "Upsets" is undefined. Nothing says what TIC-405 does when its secondary leaves cascade. Without output tracking it will wind up. There is no bumpless return path. | Specify TIC-405 behavior when FIC-420 is not in CAS: TIC-405 goes to IMAN and tracks the FIC-420 setpoint. Specify the return sequence. Delete "during upsets." |
| R-05 | Whole section | There are no requirement IDs and no test methods. | Assign FR-C401-NNN to each requirement and give each one a test method. |
| R-06 | ¶1, LIC-411 → FIC-410 | The cascade gives no mode behavior, no action, and no response to bad PV on LT-411 or FT-410. | Add action, shed modes, and bad-PV response for both loops. |
| R-07 | ¶1, FIC-412 | "Fixed operator setpoint" gives no limits. With reflux on drum level, the operator sets distillate rate directly. | Reference operator setpoint limits in the setpoint list. State that FIC-412 is a standalone AUTO loop. |
| R-08 | ¶3, LIC-402 → FV-402 | The tag prefix is inconsistent. An FV valve implies a flow controller FIC-402, but the level controller drives the valve directly. Either a FIC-402 cascade is missing, or the valve is LV-402. | Check the instrument index and P&ID. Correct the tag or add the cascade. |
| R-09 | ¶3, ¶4 | Controller action is not stated for LIC-402, LIC-411, or PIC-430. For hot vapor bypass, the action depends on the PV-430 fail position and on the process effect (opening the bypass raises drum pressure). | State the PV direction and output direction for each loop. Tie this to the fail positions (R-10). |
| R-10 | Whole section | No fail positions for FV-410, FV-412, FV-420, FV-402, or PV-430. | Reference fail positions from the instrument index. State the resulting process response for each. |
| R-11 | Whole section | Comms loss and power loss/restart behavior are not defined, including restart mode and output for each loop. | Add an abnormal-handling section, or reference the control philosophy section that covers it. |
| R-12 | ¶4, PIC-430 | There is no reference to high-pressure overrides, interlocks, or SIS functions. A pressure-related SIF on C-401 or the reboiler steam supply is likely. | Reference the C&E chart and SRS SIF numbers. Do not restate them. |
| R-13 | Whole section | No alarms are referenced, for example TIC-405 deviation, bad PV, mode shed, or level/pressure limits. | Reference the rationalized alarm database entries. |
| R-14 | ¶2, "Tray 5" | The tray numbering convention (top-down or bottom-up) is not stated. This matters for a debutanizer temperature control tray. | Reference the tray numbering on the process datasheet, or state it. |
| R-15 | Section scope | No states or transitions are shown: startup, total reflux, normal, shutdown. | Confirm that Section 3 covers these. If not, add an ISA-106 state table and define loop modes in each state. |
| R-16 | ¶6, ¶7 | STE: "should" and "may" are not imperative, and "approximately" is vague. | Fix in the rewrite. Run the STE pass after the engineering content is settled. |

## Suggested rewrite (engineering content only; STE pass to follow)

> **5.1 Column Control**
>
> Tuning values are in the C-401 tuning sheet, [doc no./rev — **open item**]. Setpoint and output limits are in the C-401 setpoint list. Fail positions are in the instrument index.
>
> | ID | Requirement | Test method |
> |---|---|---|
> | FR-C401-001 | FIC-410 controls reflux flow. In CAS, LIC-411 sets the FIC-410 setpoint. | FAT: step LIC-411 output, verify FIC-410 SP tracks |
> | FR-C401-002 | LIC-411 action: when LT-411 increases, LIC-411 increases the FIC-410 setpoint. | FAT: simulated PV step, verify direction |
> | FR-C401-003 | FIC-412 controls distillate flow in AUTO at an operator setpoint. The DCS limits the setpoint to the range in the setpoint list. | FAT: enter SP outside the limits, verify rejection |
> | FR-C401-004 | TIC-405 controls the tray 5 temperature (tray numbering per [datasheet]). In CAS, TIC-405 sets the FIC-420 setpoint. | FAT: verify cascade link |
> | FR-C401-005 | TIC-405 is reverse acting: when TT-405 increases, TIC-405 decreases the FIC-420 setpoint. | FAT: simulated PV step, verify direction |
> | FR-C401-006 | When FIC-420 is not in CAS, TIC-405 goes to IMAN and its output tracks the FIC-420 setpoint. | FAT: put FIC-420 in AUTO/MAN, verify TIC-405 tracking and no windup |
> | FR-C401-007 | When FIC-420 returns to CAS, the transfer is bumpless. | FAT: verify no step in FIC-420 SP on return |
> | FR-C401-008 | When TT-405 is bad PV, TIC-405 goes to MAN and holds its last good output. FIC-420 stays in CAS at that setpoint. The bad-PV alarm is per the alarm database [tag]. | FAT: force bad quality, verify mode, held output, alarm |
> | FR-C401-009 | After TT-405 returns to good quality, TIC-405 stays in MAN until the operator selects AUTO. | FAT: restore quality, verify no automatic return |
> | FR-C401-010 | LIC-402 controls bottoms level through [FV-402 / LV-402 — **open item R-08**]. Action: [TBD per R-09]. | FAT |
> | FR-C401-011 | PIC-430 controls column pressure through hot vapor bypass PV-430. Action: [TBD per R-09 and PV-430 fail position]. | FAT |
> | FR-C401-012 | Interlocks and SIS functions on C-401 are in C&E [doc] and SRS [SIF nos.]. This narrative does not specify them. | Document review |
>
> Bad PV, comms loss, and restart behavior for FIC-410, LIC-411, FIC-412, FIC-420, LIC-402, and PIC-430 are **open items** (R-06, R-11).

FR-C401-008 and 009 are a proposed design (MAN with held output, no automatic return). The process engineer and operations need to confirm them. An alternative is to shed FIC-420 to AUTO at its last setpoint.

## Open items

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the current TIC-405 tuning sheet revision and remove the tuning values from the narrative (R-02) | Controls lead | Before IFC |
| 2 | Confirm the TIC-405 action and correct the text (R-01) | Process engineer | Before IFC |
| 3 | Resolve the FV-402 / LV-402 tag and whether a FIC-402 cascade exists (R-08) | Process / instrument engineer | Before IFC |
| 4 | Define controller actions and fail positions for all loops (R-09, R-10) | Process engineer | Before IFC |
| 5 | Define bad PV, comms loss, and restart behavior for all loops (R-06, R-11) | Process + controls | Before IFC |
| 6 | Add C&E, SRS, and alarm database references (R-12, R-13) | Controls lead | Before IFC |
| 7 | Confirm the tray numbering convention (R-14) | Process engineer | Before IFC |
| 8 | Operations sign-off on TIC-405 / FIC-420 mode behavior and prompts | Operations | Before IFC |

Owners and dates are placeholders. Assign named owners and calendar dates before the document is issued.
